research_question: Given the buggy function and its agent-visible behavioral task/specification, can the frozen RAW Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct model generate, on its FIRST and ONLY attempt, a regression test that (a) is executable, (b) FAILS the buggy implementation for the intended behavioral reason, and (c) PASSES the accepted R3.2 verified repair (R_fix_C)?
claims_boundary: This probe measures regression-test generation ONLY: given an agent-visible task statement (title + description, faithfully rendered, no harness-authored behavioral spec) and the buggy source, can the frozen RAW model author an executable pytest regression test that exposes the bug on the first attempt? It does NOT measure: debugger success, repair generation, autonomous discovery of the specification, or correctness based solely on the generated test. The independent EvaluationVerifier remains the final correctness authority over the frozen F2P/P2P contract; the model-generated test is additional professor-facing evidence and never replaces it. A single-attempt failure at any stage leaves R4 OPEN with the first causal boundary recorded; no retry, no prompt tuning, no second model request is used to rescue the primary result.

spec_section.note: The model-facing task/spec section is rendered ONLY from task.agent_visible_mapping() title + description fields (R4 amendment 1). No harness-authored behavioral spec is added; facts not present in the agent-visible task (e.g., non-positive/empty behavior) are NOT supplied. The exact rendered section and its SHA-256 are recorded in evidence. The harness does not decide the regression assertion for the model.
